## Motor drug therapy

- [statement] CREXONT contains immediate-release carbidopa/levodopa granules and extended-release levodopa pellets, combining rapid and sustained delivery within an oral capsule. (high confidence) — https://crexont.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/CREXONT-Full-Prescribing-Information-August-2024.pdf · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] COMT inhibition reduces levodopa conversion to 3-O-methyldopa and increases levodopa availability; it is an adjunct mechanism that depends on levodopa treatment. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/ · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists

## Disease-modification research

- [statement] The LUMA primary endpoint was time to confirmed worsening in the MDS-UPDRS Parts II and III combined score. (high confidence) — https://investors.biogen.com/news-releases/news-release-details/biogen-and-denali-therapeutics-provide-update-phase-2b-luma · keywords: LRRK2-targeted therapies: small molecule and antisense
- [statement] Buntanetap, formerly Posiphen, is described as a small molecule that inhibits translation of aggregation-prone proteins including APP, tau and α-synuclein; Alzforum notes Posiphen reportedly blocks translation of α-synuclein mRNA. (high confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s44400-026-00148-x · keywords: Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap

## Rehabilitation and adjunct therapies

- [statement] The PD COMM pilot trial reported a trend to improvement in the Voice Handicap Index at three months with both LSVT LOUD and standard speech and language therapy versus control, whereas the full PD COMM trial reported benefit for LSVT LOUD but no evidence of benefit for NHS speech and language therapy versus no therapy. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5763537/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy
- [statement] The complementary-medicine clinical practice guideline for idiopathic PD (Cho et al.) grades concomitant use of acupuncture and anti-parkinsonian drug therapy as 'should be considered' (strength of recommendation B, level of evidence low; twenty-one RCTs) and moxibustion as 'may be considered' (strength C, level of evidence low). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6196228/ · keywords: Acupuncture, massage and traditional adjuncts in PD

## Surgical and device therapies

- [statement] External pumps require daily preparation and site or tube care, often with caregiver support; DBS exchanges this daily external-pump burden for neurosurgery and continuing device follow-up. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592668/ · keywords: Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS
- [statement] For persistent stimulation-related adverse effects, the programming review recommends checking electrode location, reducing stimulation current and/or changing the active contact; alternative configurations can restrict current spread. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558426/ · keywords: Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming

## Lifestyle and supportive care

- [statement] The Parkinson’s Foundation recommends discussing an in-home occupational-therapy Home Safety Evaluation with the doctor to obtain personalized recommendations. (low confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/management/activities-daily-living/home-safety · keywords: Fall prevention, home safety and mobility aids in PD
- [statement] Caregiver burden describes adverse effects on caregivers’ physical, emotional, social and financial well-being; it should be assessed as the care partner’s own experience rather than equated with the person with PD being a burden. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10802092/ · keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD

## Non-motor symptoms

- [statement] Apathy involves diminished motivation and goal-directed behavior and can occur independently of depression; its characteristic indifference differs from depressive dysphoria or hopelessness, despite overlap between the syndromes. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12261265/ · keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy
- [statement] PD sleep complaints require separate assessment of insomnia, REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD), and excessive daytime sleepiness; results on overall sleep quality should not be assumed to establish efficacy for each phenotype. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13612690/ · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness

## Neurobiology and disease landscape

- [statement] The task force recommends the term early-onset Parkinson’s disease rather than young-onset Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9547138/ · keywords: Sex, age and ancestry differences and young-onset PD
- [statement] The reviews describe alpha-synuclein as a protein concentrated at presynaptic nerve terminals. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8347623/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein biology and prion-like spread

## Diagnosis and biomarkers

- [statement] DaTscan uses iodine-123 ioflupane SPECT to visualize striatal dopamine transporter availability; it is an adjunct to other diagnostic evaluations rather than a standalone disease identification test. (medium confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/022454s010lbl.pdf · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] A Viewpoint cautions against premature adoption of the alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay as a Parkinson disease biomarker test in general neurology practice; this is an attributed clinical-implementation caution. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39102226/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

## Frontier platforms

- [statement] The biomarker review states that its proportions describe the sample assessed, not the entire PD machine learning literature, and an earlier review likewise describes its work as sampling current ML practices in PD applications. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13702696/ · keywords: AI and machine learning in PD diagnosis and progression

## Research ecosystem and health systems

- [statement] Stephenson and colleagues report that EMA issued a 2018 Qualification Opinion for DAT imaging as an enrichment biomarker in trials targeting early motor Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6700608/ · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] Yang and colleagues estimated the total economic burden of diagnosed Parkinson disease in the United States in 2017 at $51.9 billion. (low confidence) (verified as of 2020-07-09) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7347582/ · keywords: Global burden, economic cost and access to PD care
